Accountable for facilitating and coordinating the provision of confidential, high-quality support, secretarial and executive administrative services and project work to ensure the efficient operation of the office of Heath Protection and Regulation (HPR).

The position provides executive assistant services for the Executive Director HPR and is required to liaise extensively with high-level stakeholders, identify, prioritise and address a range of issues, including media queries and requests, and develop, implement and monitor systems to enhance the administrative services within the office.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 943982

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment)

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact)

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Job Title: Mobile Physiotherapist  

  Location:  NorthEast Melbourne 
 Employment Type:  Full-time / Part-time / Casual 

  About the Role  
We are looking for a dedicated and compassionate Physiotherapist to join a growing allied health team delivering high-quality, home-based care. This is a mobile role where you will work directly with clients in their own environments, helping them regain independence, improve mobility, and achieve their health goals. 

 This opportunity offers a high level of flexibility, allowing you to design a schedule that suits your lifestyle while still making a meaningful impact on patients’ lives. 

  Key Responsibilities  

 
	 Conduct in-home physiotherapy assessments and develop tailored treatment plans 
	 Deliver evidence-based rehabilitation programs focused on functional outcomes 
	 Support clients with a wide range of conditions including post-surgical recovery, neurological, and chronic conditions 
	 Monitor progress and adapt treatment plans as needed 
	 Maintain accurate clinical documentation and reports 
	 Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team and communicate with relevant stakeholders 
 

  Client Base  
You will work with a diverse caseload, including individuals requiring: 

 
	 Post-acute and post-surgical rehabilitation 
	 Neurological and cardio-respiratory care 
	 Pre- and post-natal support 
	 General mobility and independence improvement 
 

 Clients are typically treated in their homes, supporting recovery in a comfortable and familiar environment. 

  What We’re Looking For  

 
	 Bachelor’s degree in Physiotherapy (or higher) 
	 Full professional registration 
	 Minimum of 2 years’ clinical experience 
	 Strong interpersonal and communication skills 
	 Ability to work independently in a mobile setting 
	 Valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle 
	 Commitment to delivering patient-centered, high-quality care 
 

  What’s on Offer  

 
	 Flexible working arrangements—choose your own schedule 
	 Supportive and collaborative team culture 
	 Ongoing professional development, mentoring, and training 
	 Strong administrative support to reduce paperwork 
	 Opportunities for career growth within a rapidly expanding organisation 
	 Access to a diverse and engaging caseload 
 

 The organization is committed to empowering clinicians to focus on what they do best—providing exceptional care—while being fully supported by an experienced team and efficient systems   Apply Now

Hays Brisbane | Public Sector Project Engineer    Your new company     
 Join a large local government organisation supporting the delivery of essential civil infrastructure projects across the Brisbane region. You will be part of a busy construction team responsible for delivering projects safely, efficiently and in line with agreed budgets, timeframes and quality standards. 
   Your new role     
 As a Project Engineer, you will assist with the delivery of assigned civil construction projects and programs of work. You will work closely with Construction and Delivery Managers to support project planning, procurement, contractor management, risk management and technical delivery. 
 Your responsibilities will include managing project costs, monitoring schedules, supporting procurement and contract delivery, providing technical advice, coordinating quality assurance processes and ensuring projects are delivered to scope, budget and safety requirements. 
 This is a contract opportunity until 25 June 2027, based from Carina Heights with work across various project locations. 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Tertiary qualification in Engineering. 
 Current C Class driver's licence. 
 Current White Card or equivalent construction safety competency. 
 Strong technical knowledge in civil engineering, construction management and procurement. 
 Experience delivering and managing civil construction projects. 
 Ability to apply WHS, environmental and quality policies in an operational field environment. 
 Experience using Microsoft Project, SAP, works management systems and general office software. 
 Strong communication skills with the ability to liaise with technical and non-technical stakeholders. 
 
   What you'll get in return     
 
 Contract opportunity through to June 2027. 
 5 x 8-hour days, with a maximum 40-hour work week. 
 Opportunity to work on civil construction projects that support essential community infrastructure. 
 Exposure to project delivery, procurement, contractor management and quality assurance. 
 Work within a supportive construction team across varied project sites. 
 Depot based at Carina Heights with work across various locations. 
 
   What you need to do now     
 If you're interested in this role, forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call now.
